# The generated resonant interaction is on the irrelevant side

The finite-cell identities in this file are exact algebraic reductions.
Their coefficients are evaluated numerically and independently matched
to physical-word matrices. The infrared conclusion is at the usual
perturbative weak-coupling RG standard, not a microscopic CFT theorem.

## The quartic is generated by the literal port

In the legal code let R0 be the inverse of the sum of the two charged
carrier Hamiltonians. Let C be the sum of their conversion operators,
with the factor g removed. Let S0 be the literal port source with
lambda alpha² removed. In species order AA,AB,BA,BB it has components
`(0,-P_left,I,0)` at pair positions `(s-1,0)`.

The exact second-order-in-port coefficient is

```
K(g)=-S0^dagger (R0^(-1)+g C)^(-1) S0
    =K0+g² K2+g⁴ K4+O(g⁶),
K_(2r)=-S0^dagger R0 (C R0)^(2r) S0.                   (1)
```

Odd terms vanish because the species do not return to the source.
K0 is scalar. K2 is Gaussian on the **entire** pair Fock space, with
hopping T in SYMBOL.md and cancelling combined onsite terms. K4 has
nonzero quartics. No independent interaction sign or amplitude is
chosen. At order lambda² distinct physical bonds cannot return the
excited tokens to the code, so the many-cell coefficient is the sum
of these pair bonds. Higher port orders are a separate error budget.

For n=2 the pair code has 16 states and the literal excited-pair
resolvent has dimension 1024. For n=3 these dimensions are 64 and
6400. The independently assembled literal matrices agree with (1)
through K4 to less than 5e-17 in the recorded checks. Reconstruction
from the constant, quadratic and quartic pieces reproduces K4 on
the full Fock space; it is not a fit only to two-particle levels.

There is also a finite-cell remainder bound. The charged gap is
`delta=2-2cos(pi/(s+1))`, `||R0||=1/(2delta)`,
`||C||<=2`, and `||S0||=sqrt(2)`. For |g|<delta,

```
||K(g)-K0-g²K2-g⁴K4||
 <= (1/delta) (|g|/delta)^6 / [1-(g/delta)²].           (2)
```

This controls the coefficient at fixed cell size. It is not the missing
volume-uniform low-energy reduction of the full gapless chain.

## Band-basis matching, including direct and exchange contributions

Write the normal-ordered quartic part as

```
K4_quartic=sum_(i<j,k<l) W_(ij),(kl) f_i^dagger f_j^dagger f_l f_k,
```

where i,j,k,l label the four modes of the two adjacent cells.
W is extracted by subtracting the vacuum and one-particle reconstruction
from the two-particle block. Its reconstruction is then tested in every
particle sector. The complete W, not only selected entries, is saved.

For a normalized Bloch eigenvector u_a at k_a define the two-cell wave
`w_a=(u_a,exp(i k_a)u_a)` and its wedge
`v_ab,ij=w_a,i w_b,j-w_a,j w_b,i`. Then the continuum coefficient is

```
Gamma_(ab;cd)=v_ab^dagger W v_cd.                      (3)
```

This formula antisymmetrizes both incoming and outgoing particles.
It uses the actual Bloch eigenvectors, never the nonunitarily whitened
ones used to prove the root identity.

Choose channel 1 as R1=root 0, L1=root 3, and channel 2 as R2=root 2,
L2=root 1, using SYMBOL.md's ordering. The coefficients below multiply
`lambda² alpha⁴ g⁴=t0 g²`; the velocities multiply t0.

| Quantity | Coefficient |
|---|---:|
| v1 | .000194934017243605 |
| v2 | .000464058241424723 |
| G1, rho_R1 rho_L1 | .000760820792042557 |
| G2, rho_R2 rho_L2 | .002121136908838399 |
| Gx, rho_R1 rho_L2 and rho_R2 rho_L1 | .000780347649099188 |
| Same-chiral cross density coupling | .000855203949209884 |
| Pair-transfer magnitude | .000074856300110693 |

J multiplies `psi_R1^dagger psi_L1^dagger psi_L2 psi_R2+h.c.`.
Its sign depends on the pair ordering and field phases; its magnitude
and stability criterion do not. In particular, it is **not zero** and
is not protected by a separate microscopic U(1) for each channel.

The root-pair audit leaves only these forward channels and pair transfer
among marginal quartics. No extra umklapp is silently omitted. At weak
coupling, six-fermion and derivative operators have dimension above two;
number-nonconserving vertices are excluded by the exact physical charge.

## Forward dimensions and the full leading one-loop test

Let G1,G2,Gx,J now denote physical continuum couplings and v1,v2 their
positive velocities. Define

```
D=G1/(2pi v1)+G2/(2pi v2)-2Gx/[pi(v1+v2)],
B=1/(2pi² v1 v2)+2/[pi²(v1+v2)²],   Y=sqrt(B)|J|.      (4)
```

The pair-transfer scaling dimension at the forward-scattering fixed
point is `2+D+O(G²)`. For example, the bosonic stiffness correction
obeys `delta K_ij=-G_ij/[pi(v_i+v_j)]`; applying `K^-1` to (1,-1)
gives (4). Same-chiral forward scattering shifts velocities and does
not enter this first-order dimension. A positive bare D alone would
not settle stability, because J feeds back into the forward couplings.

With `ell=log(initial cutoff/current cutoff)`, the needed flows are

```
dG1/dell=-|J|²/(2pi v2),
dG2/dell=-|J|²/(2pi v1),
dGx/dell=+|J|²/[pi(v1+v2)],
dJ/dell=-D J.
```

They reproduce the one-component specialization of Szirmai--Solyom,
[Eqs. (21), (23)--(25), (27)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0605300).
Their parallel-spin convention is minus the density coupling here:
`g_parallel^a=-G1/(2pi v1)`, `g_parallel^ab=-Gx/[pi(v1+v2)]`;
the charge-transfer coupling is J divided by `pi(v1+v2)`, up to its
unphysical sign. Reversing their log-cutoff direction gives the flows
above. This explicit conversion fixes the sign and factor-of-two issue.

To leading order, holding the velocities at their noninteracting values,

```
dD/dell=-Y²,  dY/dell=-D Y,  D²-Y²=constant.            (5)
```

Thus `D>|Y|` is an open irrelevant basin: Y flows to zero and D tends
to a positive value. For the literal seed,

```
D=.594793189805 g²+O(g⁴),
Y=.075847395825 g²+O(g⁴),
D-Y=.518945793980 g²+O(g⁴),
D²-Y²=.348026111185 g⁴+O(g⁶).                          (6)
```

The generated resonance therefore **decays**, within this controlled
leading weak-coupling flow; it does not lock the relative mode. Nine
nearby sampled root designs have leading D-Y at least .15539 g².
Strict positivity at the primary point gives an open neighbourhood by
continuity; a finite grid is not an interval arithmetic certificate.

Under the stated infrared matching and weak-coupling RG assumptions,
the remaining two positive-velocity Gaussian modes give total Virasoro
c=2. This is an interacting continuum prediction, not a count inferred
solely from four roots. Higher-order coefficients at fixed n are smaller
as g tends to zero, but a rigorous microscopic CFT result still requires
the sector and matching work in LIMITS.md. No claimed universal c bound
or arbitrary-c family follows from (6).
